test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-2) Official Paper (Held On: 16 June 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Who among the following is the author of the famous book 'Rihla' which provides extremely rich and interesting details about the social and cultural life of the Indian subcontinent in the fourteenth century?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ibn Battuta.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rihla**

 
 
• **The Arabic word** for a **journey or the travelogue that documents it**. 
 
• Formal title **A Masterpiece** to **Those Who Contemplate the Wonders of Cities and the Marvels of Travelling.**
 
• This book is a travelogue documenting his** lifetime of travel and exploration, which according to his description covered about 70,000 miles.**
 
• **Original Language: Arabic**
 
 
 
• **Ibn Battuta**
 
 
• **Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Battutah.**
 
• He was a **Berber Maghrebi scholar and explorer who travelled extensively in the lands of Afro-Eurasia, largely in the Muslim world.**
 
• He **came to India during the reign of Muhammad bin-Tughlaq.**
 
• **He travelled around 117,000 km in pre-modern history.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Al-Biruni**

 
 
• One of the most** important Muslim authorities in the history of religion.**
 
• Also known as **"founder of Indology", "Father of Comparative Religion", "Father of modern geodesy", and the first anthropologist.**
 
• **Nationality: Iranian**
 
 
 
• **Francois Bernier**
 
 
• **French physician and traveller.**
 
• He was** associated with the Mughal Court as a personal physician of Dara Shikoh **and** later as a scientist with Danishmand Khan.**
 
 
 
• **Hiuen Tsang**
 
 
• The **7th-century Chinese Buddhist monk, scholar, traveller, and translator.**
 
• He started **translating Sanskrit texts that he brought from India and successfully completed the translation of more than 600 Buddhist texts.**
